para: The instrument of investigation is the subclassical graph of calculi: a directed graph in which every node is a logical calculus and every edge encodes a specific structural relationship between two calculi — whether one extends the other by the addition of axioms or rules, whether one embeds into the other by a definitional translation, whether the two are equivalent under some reinterpretation of their connectives, or whether one is the systematic dual of the other, obtained by exchanging the roles of premiss and conclusion in the underlying proof theory. The graph does not impose an arbitrary ordering on the calculi; it records the relationships that hold among them on structural grounds. To traverse it is, in the relevant sense, to do comparative proof theory in earnest — not as a catalogue of curiosities, but as the systematic cartography of a previously unmapped territory.
